title: Our Home is Our Inspiration
slide_intent: Teach designers to look at the place an organization inhabits before choosing an abstract form. A surface, angle or color found there can give an unfamiliar identity a specific point of reference.
strategic_value: CSAIL can tie its graphic vocabulary to a place its researchers share. The irregular volumes and contrasting materials in the Stata Center photograph give the lab a source for visual decisions beyond its name.
demonstration: A wide photograph of the Stata Center shows leaning metal faces, orange masonry, white surfaces and a yellow volume. The adjacent text identifies the building’s polygons, angles, volumes, colors and materials as sources for the identity.
practical_value: Use the photograph to select a relationship worth carrying into a graphic, such as a tilted edge against a vertical one. The later pattern page shows how the lab uses such angles in a different medium.

content_islands.name: Origin story
content_islands.spec: Set the heading and short account of the Stata Center in a narrow upper-left column. Keep its description of the building’s form beside the image.

content_islands.name: Architecture photograph
content_islands.spec: Give the large right field to a single photograph. Keep enough of the building in the frame to show relationships between neighboring volumes, colors and surfaces.

content_islands.name: Brand statement
content_islands.spec: Place a short orange rule and italic orange statement near the foot of the left column, apart from the origin story.

content_islands.name: Book footer
content_islands.spec: Align the short-guide identifier, laboratory name and folio along the bottom margin.
